title: quant-surface-optimizer-prefill-lane-coordinator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a runtime component (Quant Surface Optimizer) that coordinates head-level precision lanes during prefill and decode to reduce dequantization overhead and preserve latency SLOs. The component will: 1) analyze token distribution and KV cache reuse patterns at prefill time, 2) assign attention heads to INT8/FP8/FP16 lanes dynamically, 3) defer dequant ops where safe and overlap dequant with KV prefill/IO, and 4) expose configuration knobs for conservative vs aggressive precision consolidation. Goal: reduce average per-token CPU/GPU overhead from dequant by >=20% on mixed-precision workloads while keeping 95th-percentile decode latency within 1.15x of baseline.
background: We currently see significant per-token overhead from eager dequantization in mixed-precision pipelines, especially on short decode paths where prefill and KV construction dominate latency. Existing kernel-selection logic picks precision per-layer but does not consider head-level heterogeneity or the opportunity to overlap dequant with prefill streaming. Prior tickets explored per-layer kernel arbitration and microkernel fusion, but didn't introduce a runtime lane allocator that coordinates dequant timing with prefill scheduling.
acceptance_criteria: Quant Surface Optimizer implemented in runtime as a pluggable module (config-driven)
Head-level lane allocator that can assign heads to INT8/FP8/FP16 per-request based on token statistics
Dequant deferral mechanism that overlaps with KV prefill and reduces visible dequant CPU/GPU stalls
Benchmarks showing >=20% reduction in mean dequant overhead and 95th-percentile decode latency <=1.15x baseline on our mixed-precision harness
Telemetry: new metrics exported (lane_assignments, dequant_deferred_ms, dequant_overlap_ms) and dashboards in Console
Integration tests and a canary rollout plan for dedicated and hosted environments
tasks: Design API surface and config flags (conservative/aggressive/auto)
Implement head-level lane allocator in serving runtime
Add dequant deferral and overlap primitives to kernel scheduler
Create microbench harness (short/long prompts, varying prefills) for INT8/FP8/FP16 combinations
Run scale experiments on dedicated pool (x10 samples) and collect telemetry
PRs: runtime module + unit tests + e2e benchmark jobs
Console dashboard: visualize lane utilization and latency impact
Write rollout playbook with rollback triggers and canary percentage schedule
risks: Aggressive deferral may cause correctness/regression for models that assume exact FP output ordering
Complexity in kernel scheduler could regress throughput under high concurrency if not carefully throttled
Telemetry blind spots if metrics aren't exported per-request leading to difficulty diagnosing regressions
Hardware variation: INT8/FP8 speedups are device-dependent (A100 vs H100 vs future GPUs)
design_notes: Quant Surface: lightweight runtime layer that sits between request planner and kernel selector; accepts head_profile and token_reuse hints
Lane allocator uses a cost model: estimated dequant cost + estimated kernel speedup when choosing lane; model coefficients calibrated from microbenchmarks
Deferred dequant implementation uses zero-copy views where possible and schedules dequant kernels to run in parallel with KV prefill writes; fallback to eager dequant for critical head pairs
Conservative mode pins heads to same precision as model rollout (min risk); auto mode toggles per-request based on runtime confidence threshold
Safety net: if gradient of latency vs quality indicates >2% generation divergence, automatically fall back to full-precision path and emit alert
experiments_plan: Microbench: measure dequant op time across INT8/FP8/FP16 for attention and matmul kernels; run with sequence lengths 8, 32, 512
Prefill overlap test: instrument timeline to measure overlap between KV writes and dequant kernels; target overlap >=60% of dequant duration
End-to-end latency: run mixed-precision decode on llama-13b-equivalent test model with 1k requests and compute mean/95th latency
Quality regression: run prompt-based eval set (200 prompts) comparing outputs against FP16 baseline; target <=0.5% pass-rate drift for auto mode
Hardware sweep: run on A100-80GB and H100-80GB; capture device-specific kernel speedups and update cost model
